\[
W(f) = F(f) \left(\frac{M}{A(|f|)}\right)^{\alpha},\quad A(r) = \operatorname{mean}_{|f| \approx r} |F(f)|,\quad \alpha = 1
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(F\): The spectrum of the extended image
- \(A(r)\): The mean magnitude on ring r
- \(M\): The mean magnitude of the whole spectrum
- \(\alpha\): The strength

The magnitude of the spectrum of a natural image falls roughly as 1 over the frequency, as Field showed. A(r) is the mean magnitude on each ring of frequencies at the same distance r from the center, and M the mean magnitude of the whole spectrum. Scaling each ring by M / A makes the rings equally strong, a flat or white spectrum. Frequency 0, the mean brightness, is kept. The strength alpha blends from no change at 0 to a flat spectrum at 1. Using the ring mean as the estimate of the magnitude is this filter's own choice. A ring holds the frequencies whose distance from the center, in steps of 1 over the larger side of the FFT grid, rounds to the same whole number.
